newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall by lunch, sentiment weak.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall by lunch, sentiment weak.

text.p: Thai stocks eased further by the midday on Thursday on persistent weak sentiment and absence of market moving news, brokers said.
"There were very few new buying orders. Foreigners were still sidelined while local investors were reluctant to take new positions," said a broker at Chao Phaya Finance and Securities.
The SET index eased 2.29 points to 550.58 at the break on thin 995 million baht turnover. The SET-50 index fell 0.18 to 39.84.
Declines led advances 152 to 54 with 76 counters remained unchanged.
Brokers said the market weakness also induced continued selling of bank and finance stocks on concern about their poor earnigns.
Siam Commercial Bank topped the active list, losing four baht to 114.

Standard and Poor's Corp on Thursday said it assigned a BBB-plus long-term and A-2 short-term counterparty ratings for senior obligations of Siam Commercial Bank's $1.5 billion global medium term note programme.
S&P also gave a BBB long-term rating to its dated subordinated debt under the same programme. It said the rating outlook of the bank was negative.
The negative outlook on Siam Commercial reflects S&P's concerns that the economic downturn and resulting asset-quality problems will be higher and more prolonged than anticipated.

"Selling of Siam Commercial Bank emerged after the S&P announcement. There was nothing new but some local investors may misunderstand that the bank's rating was downgraded," said one broker at a foreign brokerage firm. Bangkok Bank was down one at 148. -- Anuchit Nguyen (662) 652-0642
